a.xlink:title: The elapsed time from arrival to response includes waiting, host work, and model execution. The target applies to the complete request.
Requests wait when arrivals compete for busy resources. Near saturation, small increases in utilization can produce large increases in waiting.
A request may wait while the server collects a batch. This delay spends latency allowance before the model runs.
Execution includes arithmetic and moving operands. A resource bound gives a lower limit; profiling explains additional overhead.
Serialization, preprocessing, transfers, and runtime dispatch can dominate the request path even when accelerator kernels are fast.
Utilization compares offered work with available service capacity. High utilization leaves little room for variation in arrivals and execution.
Grouping requests shares fixed work and can reuse weights. It can improve capacity while adding formation delay; the useful batch is constrained by latency and memory.
Supplying operands takes time. For a fixed memory level, the transfer lower bound is bytes moved divided by bandwidth.
The arithmetic lower bound is the required operations divided by the available compute rate. Faster operand delivery cannot remove this bound.
At fixed service capacity, a higher request arrival rate raises utilization. Burstiness also matters for waiting.
Service capacity is the rate at which the system can complete work under a specified workload. The latency target constrains how much of that capacity can be used.
At small decode batches, repeatedly reading model weights can dominate execution. Sharing a weight stream across requests amortizes that traffic.
Bandwidth limits the rate at which an accelerator receives operands from a given memory level. The relevant level depends on data placement and reuse.
Lower precision reduces the bytes needed for weights. It improves runtime only when the execution regime and kernel support let those saved bytes matter.
Operations per byte moved identifies the compute-versus-bandwidth regime. A suitable batch can reuse weights and raise this ratio.
